Resolves #19296

Dock hosts can now select return or retain for a native workspace. `WorkspaceSet.returnWorkspace` prepares every pane from paired queue-head captures; `NativeVesselTransaction` observes physical closure and replays native effects. Generic managers retain opaque binding/lease ownership. Workstation consumes these seams and deletes its version/retry loop, popup replay override and controller lease listener: 173 source lines removed, 67 presentation/policy lines added.

Evidence: L3 real headed Chrome and semantic/runtime controls → L3 required. No acceptance residual.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Generic managers contain no Dock imports, app identifiers or tab-placement branches; source boundary above. |
| AC-2 | `DockWorkspaceSetTransaction.spec.mjs`: ordered all-pane return, intervening writes, successor/rebind fences, empty target, refusal and compensation. |
| AC-3 | `NativeLifecycle.spec.mjs` and `DockNativeVesselTransaction.spec.mjs`: exact released binding, unknown observation, expiry while pending, warm rebind, never-bound expiry and full-promise deduplication. |
| AC-4 | Native replay refusal/successor controls; both independent-host and Workstation browser return/undo/redo retain pane identities and the existing row. |
| AC-5 | Removed app orchestration as counted above; controller opening is a shared callable. |
| AC-6 | Headed independent fixture exercises return and retain; seven headed Workstation close/reload/history/identity checks pass. |
| AC-7 | Finalized ticket ledger, callable JSDoc, Dock window guide/example and app README; default null retains the prior consumer path. |

## Deltas from ticket

Close-policy-only hosts need no tear-out gesture handlers. Dock capture stamps include lineage plus generation; `getBinding` now exposes the lineage token. Ordered result `itemIds` supports history depth zero. The existing `returnPopupWorkspace` history label stays compatible.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — Public close-policy hooks and participant seams add 50 code lines; reduction and native transactions stay in existing collaborators, while Workstation's duplicated orchestration shrinks by 106 source lines.

## Test Evidence

Headed Chrome: `DockNativeWorkspaceReturnNL` 2/2; `WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL` 3/3; four reload/cursor arms of `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` 4/4. The independent fixture uses arbitrary keys and public seams, with actual window close/reload, archived paired endpoints, render-boundary identity reads, undo and redo. Native/refusal and stale-binding controls run in CI unit specs.

Changed Mermaid rendered and inspected. Change class: capability. agent-preflight: not hosted here; shared baseline runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Confirm the shared native-close policy remains correct in the installed consumer after its Engine pin updates.

Authored by Euclid (GPT-6.1 Sol, Codex). Session 01a0ee37-7eaa-7d52-9869-ba5d0de51b43.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] **RA-1 — Make the Group owner the only writer of its binding record.**
  - **What:** `NativeVesselTransaction.releaseWorkspace` writes `binding.awaitingClosure` (`NativeVesselTransaction.mjs:62`, `:90`) and reads `binding.leaseExpired` (`:67`, `:71`, `:78`) on the manager's internal record. `NativeLifecycle#onRelease` writes the same field again from the returned disposition (`NativeLifecycle.mjs:347`).
  - **Why it is a boundary issue:** #19296 put any generic lifecycle hook "with the existing Group owner", carrying "opaque identities".
  - **Why the writes look redundant:**
    - The early write only routes a mid-observation expiry into `bindingExpired`, which joins the same pending promise.
    - The pending work re-reads expiry itself after its `await`.
    - A settled `{awaitingClosure: true}` is written by the owner anyway.
  - **Required:**
    - Drop the direct writes, and compute the refusal-path value at `:85` locally.
    - Read expiry through the owner, e.g. an `isLeaseExpired(data)` beside `isCurrentRelease`.
    - Empirical isolation test: run `DockNativeVesselTransaction.spec`, `NativeLifecycle.spec` and `DockNativeWorkspaceReturnNL` with lines 62 and 90 stripped.
    - If a path does need the flag earlier, expose it as a `NativeLifecycle` method, not a record write.
- [ ] **RA-2 — Pass `null`, not `undefined`, for an unrecorded placement.**
  - **What:** `WorkspaceSet.mjs:328` hands `placements[itemId]` to `resolveReturnDescriptor`. For an item with no recorded home that is `undefined`.
  - **Why it matters:** the resolver's documented contract is `{Object|null}`, "or null": `Workspace#resolveDockReturnDescriptor` (`Workspace.mjs:1277`), `Operations.appendingReturnDescriptor`, and `foldPlacements`' `(document, itemId, placement|null)`.
  - **The replaced path honored it:** Workstation went through `peekPlacement`, which returns `placements[itemId] || null`.
  - **Why it passes today anyway:** both shipped resolvers only test truthiness. Neo reserves `undefined` for the initial state, though, and an override checking `placement === null` would diverge.
  - **Required:** `placements[itemId] ?? null`, plus one arm asserting the resolver receives `null` for an unrecorded item.
- [ ] **RA-3 — Put `WorkspaceSet#getParticipantForBinding` in the ledger.**
  - Add it to #19296's ledger with its null-for-missing-or-ambiguous contract.
  - Or mark it `@protected`, if only `NativeVesselTransaction` is meant to call it.
